Christ: Extreme Humility

Icons

Christ

Christ: Extreme Humility

Man of Sorrows · Akra Tapeinosis

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Philippians 2:7–8

Isaiah 53:3–5

King James Version · Scripture previews

Extreme Humility is represented here by a historical Man of Sorrows icon. The Byzantine and Christian Museum describes this iconographic theme through the dead Christ standing within the sarcophagus, rather than through a scene of the soldiers mocking him.

[1] Object description, first sentences

What is depicted

In the museum’s account of Nikolaos Tzafouris’s example, Christ wears a loincloth and crosses his hands low on the body. The museum calls it a simple version of a Byzantine composition that can also include the Virgin and St. John the Evangelist.

[1] Object description: figure and related versions

History and tradition

The displayed image is catalogued as a Man of Sorrows by Nikolaos Tzafouris. It shows Christ’s closed eyes, wounds and crossed hands above the tomb. The reproduction retains the historical panel’s worn surface and painted frame.

[2] Displayed work; file-page title and description

The museum places the wider composition’s popularity between the fourteenth and sixteenth centuries. Its catalogue describes the type; that description is not a new instruction for prayer or a claim that every variant has identical details.

[1] Object description, final sentence

Published explanation

But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.

[3] Philippians 2:7–8

Image details

Man of Sorrows (Tzafouris).png

The style was very popular in Crete towards the end of the 1400s. The Greek name of the work is Akra Takinosi (Άκρα Ταπείνωση).
